title: Supply squeeze, material costs up: Nickel Q2 2026 Price Review
gist: Benchmark's Q2 2026 nickel review shows EXW China nickel sulphate up 4.8% to $4,847/tonne and mixed hydroxide precipitate (MHP) up 7.8% to $9,045/tonne, driven by tight upstream supply and elevated sulphur costs rather than a demand recovery, with analyst Frederick Bloomfield forecasting a more bearish Q3 as supply constraints ease.

insights.claim: Nickel sulphate prices (EXW China) rose 4.8% during Q2 2026, from RMB 31,250/tonne ($4,594) to RMB 32,750/tonne ($4,847).
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Concrete quarter-on-quarter benchmark for battery-grade nickel sulphate — useful for modelling nickel cost inputs into cathode precursor pricing.
insights.locator: "Benchmark's EXW China nickel sulphate price rose by 4.8%..."

insights.claim: Mixed hydroxide precipitate (MHP) prices rose 7.8% in Q2 2026, with aggregate prices reaching $9,045/tonne.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: MHP outpacing sulphate gains signals tighter upstream intermediate supply relative to refined product, relevant for battery precursor cost forecasting.

insights.claim: The Q2 2026 nickel intermediate price gains were driven by supply-side constraints and cost pressure rather than a genuine recovery in downstream nickel demand, while weaker LME nickel prices and cautious downstream buying capped further upside.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Because the rally is supply- not demand-led, it may be fragile — investors should watch demand-side indicators rather than assume price strength reflects EV/battery demand recovery.

insights.claim: Frederick Bloomfield, a senior price analyst at Benchmark, said Q2 2026 was characterised by tight upstream supply and cost pressure from elevated sulphur costs and policy uncertainty, rather than a meaningful recovery in nickel demand.
insights.speaker: Frederick Bloomfield, senior price analyst at Benchmark
insights.so_what: A direct analyst attribution confirming the rally's supply-side (not demand-side) origin, useful for distinguishing genuine EV demand recovery from cost-push price moves.
insights.quote: Overall, Q2 was characterised by tight upstream supply and cost pressure stemming from elevated sulphur costs and policy uncertainty, rather than a meaningful recovery in nickel demand

insights.claim: Frederick Bloomfield forecasts a more bearish nickel outlook for Q3 2026, as the supply constraints that supported Q2 prices are expected to be at least partially alleviated.
insights.speaker: Frederick Bloomfield, senior price analyst at Benchmark
insights.so_what: A direct forecast that nickel intermediate prices could soften in Q3 as supply eases — actionable for hedging or positioning decisions in nickel-exposed names.
insights.quote: Prices ended the quarter supported by heightened raw material costs and supply risks, but face a more bearish outlook for Q3 where supply constraints are expected to be at least partially alleviated.
